topic: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem: Fairness in a Divided World
target_audience: University students with a background in basic calculus and set theory

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Continuous Mapping
lecture_lines: Continuous mapping links spheres to flat spaces.
Imagine stretching a globe onto a plane.
We must do this without any tearing.
animations: 1. Create a 3D sphere object (color: #FFFFFF).
2. Label the sphere 'Sⁿ' (color: #FF00FF).
3. Create a flat plane representing Rⁿ (color: #00FFFF).
4. Animate the sphere surface flattening onto the plane without tearing (continuous mapping).
5. Highlight the mapped region on the plane in a different color (#FFFF00).

sections.title: The Borsuk-Ulam Theorem (The Core Concept)
lecture_lines: Borsuk-Ulam states spheres map to R-n.
Antipodal points share the same value.
Earth has two opposite spots with identical weather.
animations: 1. Render a 3D sphere with an antipodal point pair highlighted (#FF0000).
2. Label the antipodal points 'x' and '-x'.
3. Display the mapping function f: Sⁿ -> Rⁿ.
4. Visually move the pair 'x' and '-x' across the surface.
5. Flash the points when they reach identical values on Rⁿ (#00FF00).

sections.title: Transition: From Geometry to Combinatorics
lecture_lines: Topology helps us solve discrete problems.
Necklaces represent linear, ordered resource sets.
Cuts divide these sets into fair shares.
animations: 1. Display a 1D necklace composed of two bead types: gold (#FFD700) and silver (#C0C0C0).
2. Place cutting lines along the necklace (#FF0000).
3. Shift segments to visually demonstrate an equal split of bead counts.

sections.title: The Stolen Necklace Problem
lecture_lines: Two thieves split a mixed bead necklace.
K plus S cuts ensure fair division.
Each thief receives identical bead types.
Raccoons demonstrate equal distribution of resources.
Fairness is guaranteed by simple cutting math.
animations: 1. Create a necklace with 20 beads (10 gold #FFD700, 10 silver #C0C0C0).
2. Illustrate 'k+s' cuts at optimal positions (#FF0000).
3. Show two groups (raccoons) gathering the resulting necklace pieces.
4. Highlight both piles as equal in gold and silver count.
5. Confirm equality with a scale pulse on both piles (#00FF00).

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Significance
lecture_lines: Topology provides concrete guarantees for fairness.
Mathematical constraints force equitable resource allocation.
Useful for computing tasks and economics.
animations: 1. Display a summary text: 'Topology guarantees fairness'.
2. Show icons representing assets: money bags and computing servers.
3. Animate the assets being partitioned into equal groups (#00FF00).
